title: Interface Default Methods
story: Your `Playable` interface has `play()`, `pause()`, and `stop()`. But `stop()` is the same for every type: just call `pause()` then reset. Instead of making every type re-implement `stop()`, give the interface a default implementation.
why: Default methods in interfaces provide shared behavior that types can inherit without re-implementing, reducing code duplication.
analogy: A smartphone comes with default apps (calculator, calendar) that work for everyone. But you can install custom apps to replace them. Default interface methods are the built-in apps — they work out of the box, but you can override them with custom behavior.
try_it: Add a `summarize` default method that returns `label() + " (type: " + type_name() + ")"`. Add `type_name()` to the interface. Then create a `Service` type that overrides `describe()` with a custom message.
tips: Default methods should be expressible in terms of other interface methods
Types can override defaults — the override always takes priority
Use defaults for DRY: implement once in the interface, use everywhere
common_mistakes: Putting complex logic in defaults that can't be expressed via other methods
Forgetting that defaults can call other interface methods — that's their power
Overriding when the default is fine — don't override just because you can
